newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada domestic spot natgas little changed in week.
newsitem.headline: Canada domestic spot natgas little changed in week.

text.p: Canadian domestic spot natural gas prices were little changed from last week but firmer than Tuesday as temperatures in western Canada cooled and a few gas plants in Alberta began maintenance.

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.50/1.53 per gigajoule, up five cents per GJ from last week and about 10 cents from Tuesday. AECO gas for March delivery was quoted at C$1.51/1.53 per GJ, down about two cents from a week ago.
"Field receipts (on the NOVA system) were down with plant turnarounds and there's cooler weather," said one trader.
A NOVA official said he estimated about 100 million cubic feet per day of gas was off the intra-Alberta network with one 50 MMCFD plant and a series of small ones down on Wednesday.
Temperatures in southern Alberta were forecast to remain near normal until Sunday when cooler weather was expected, Environment Canada said.
At the borders, gas at Sumas, Washington was down sharply from last week amid warm weather and ample hydroelectric power generation in the U.S. Pacific Northwest, traders said.
Gas at Sumas was talked at about US$1.09 per million British thermal units, down about 20 cents from February 19.
Marketers said there was no change in prices following a declared -- then quickly lifted -- force majeure at Westcoast Energy Inc's big McMahon processing plant.
Westcoast said problems were detected in the plant's sulphur unit early on Wednesday but were cleared up about an hour later.
